# `Q-3-30` — Shortcode Not Supported

> Quarto shortcodes are not representable in this output format.

## What this means

A shortcode is a `{{{< name arg >}}}` construct that Quarto
expands during rendering — `{{{< meta title >}}}` inserts the
document title, `{{{< var key >}}}` inserts a value from
`_variables.yml`, and so on. Expansion normally happens before
the writer sees the AST.

This error fires when an unexpanded shortcode reaches the
writer. The writer cannot pass it through (the syntax is
Quarto-specific, not part of the output format), so it has no
choice but to refuse.

## Why this happens

Two known triggers:

- **The shortcode name is unknown.** Quarto's expander leaves
  unrecognized shortcodes in place rather than erasing them; the
  writer then sees the surviving node.
- **A Lua filter introduced a shortcode** after the expansion
  pass. Shortcodes added after expansion will never run.

## How to fix

Check the spelling of the shortcode name. If it is correct,
confirm that the shortcode is one Quarto provides (`meta`,
`var`, `embed`, `include`, ...) or that the relevant extension
is loaded.

For filter-introduced shortcodes, expand them inside the filter
rather than emitting the shortcode node, or move the filter
earlier in the pipeline so the expander runs again.
